cover.headline: Good assets in a bad cycle, and a share price propped up by Titan: SELL
cover.lead: Tata Chemicals is one of the world's largest soda ash makers outside China, with low-cost natural mines in the US and Kenya, an integrated Indian business, 55% of Rallis India and a portfolio of Tata-group shares. Chinese oversupply has pushed export prices to near cash cost: US EBITDA fell from ₹1,269 cr (FY23) to ₹3 cr in Q1FY27, the US goodwill was written down by ₹1,837 cr and FY26 ended in a loss after minorities. India is the only large unit earning well. We value the stock the way the street does, on the **sum of its parts (Sep-28E EV/EBITDA by geography, Rallis and the Tata-group shares at market less 20%)**. That gives **{{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}})**: **we initiate with SELL.** About ₹330 a share of value is shares the company does not control; the operations are worth ~₹233 a share after debt and pensions. Our EBITDA is far below the street because we do not assume Chinese capacity closes. Bull case {{scen.bull.tp|inr}} (soda ash recovery plus a Tata Sons listing); bear case {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.h: Soda ash: China sets the price and has too much
arguments.p: Chinese inventories are at a record 1.73 mt and export prices are US$160-180/t FOB, near cash cost. Management says US exports to South-East Asia will stay "breakeven or unremunerative" at least through FY27 and sees no uplift "unless some capacity rationalization happens in China". Volumes are fine; price is the problem.

arguments.h: India earns the money, but Q1 flattered it
arguments.p: India made ₹954 cr of EBITDA in FY26 and a record 28% margin in Q1FY27 on import-parity pricing, salt volumes and cheap coal. Management itself calls ~18% sustainable. We use 19.5-20% for FY28-29E; the street uses ~24%.

arguments.h: Half the value is somebody else's business
arguments.p: The Tata-group shares (Titan ₹6,342 cr, Indian Hotels, Tata Steel and others: ₹8,297 cr) and the Rallis stake (₹2,137 cr) are worth ₹409 a share before any discount, over half the price. They move with Titan, not with soda ash. The 2.53% Tata Sons stake is a real option (₹390+ a share at press valuations) but has no listing date; we leave it out of the base case, as the street does.

arguments.h: Valuation: priced for a recovery we do not yet see
arguments.p: At ₹611 the market pays ~7.8x our Sep-28E EBITDA for the operations; our multiples (India 8x, US 6x, others 5-8x, in the street's range) blend to 7.1x. Our FY28E EPS of ₹{{F.eps.1|n1}} compares with Motilal Oswal's ₹43; P/E is meaningless. The DCF and a group EV/EBITDA cross-check are higher, but only because they ignore pensions, minorities and holding-company discounts.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): US EBITDA per tonne after the Searles Valley contracts; whether India's Q1 margin holds as costlier coal comes through.
Indian safeguard duty on soda ash imports: DGTR investigation opened 16-Mar-2026; a decision would support domestic prices.
Tata Sons: whether it lists (RBI rejected its de-registration on 11-Sep-2026) or restructures to avoid listing (Tata Trusts proposal reported 29-Sep-2026).
Chinese soda ash capacity closures and export prices; Kenya's fuel hedge ends in October 2026.
Non-core land sales from H2FY27; 82.5 KTPA IVSD salt plant at Mithapur due by end-FY27.

sections.title: A soda ash company with a salt business, a listed agrochemical subsidiary and a share portfolio

blocks.p: Soda ash (sodium carbonate) is a white powder used to make glass (flat, container and solar glass), detergents, lithium carbonate and many chemicals. Tata Chemicals is one of the world's largest producers outside China, with 3.9 mtpa of capacity, more than two-thirds of it "natural" soda ash mined from trona in Wyoming and Kenya, which needs far less energy than the "synthetic" (Solvay process) ash made in India and China. Around soda ash it has built salt, sodium bicarbonate, prebiotics and silica businesses, owns 55% of Rallis India, a third of a Moroccan phosphoric acid plant (IMACID), and holds shares in Titan, Indian Hotels, Tata Steel and other Tata companies.

sections.title: Soda ash: China has built too much, and sets the price everywhere

blocks.p: Soda ash is a commodity: one grade sells at one world price, adjusted for freight and duty. China is the largest producer and, after years of adding capacity (including new natural soda ash in Inner Mongolia), it has far more than it needs. Its inventories reached a record 1.73 million tonnes in mid-2026, its plants still run at high utilisation, and its exporters sell at US$160-180 a tonne FOB (US$170-190 delivered in South-East Asia). Management believes most Chinese producers are losing cash at these prices and calls ~US$170 the floor, but no large Chinese closures have been announced. Until they are, every exporter, including Tata Chemicals' US and Kenyan plants, earns close to nothing on export tonnes.

sections.title: India: the only big unit earning its keep, helped by import parity

blocks.p: The Indian (standalone) business makes soda ash, salt, bicarb, prebiotics (scFOS), silica, bromine and cement at Mithapur, Mambattu and Cuddalore. FY26 revenue was ₹4,831 cr (+9%) and EBITDA ₹954 cr (19.7%), helped by the FY25 expansions: Mithapur produced 1 mtpa of soda ash for the first time and bicarb capacity doubled to 290 KTPA. Q1FY27 was exceptional: revenue +10% to ₹1,281 cr, EBITDA +35% to ₹364 cr (28.4%), from 20% higher salt volumes, a ~₹2,000/t soda ash price increase (domestic prices track import parity, so a weaker rupee lifts them) and cheap coal in inventory.

Asked for a sustainable margin, the CEO said "around 18%".

**Salt for Tata Consumer:** much of the salt goes to Tata Consumer Products (Tata Salt) under the arrangement set at the 2020 demerger; management says terms are unchanged. Steady volumes, limited pricing power.
**Soda ash pricing:** contracts are reset quarterly against import parity. The pending safeguard duty would support prices; a stronger rupee or falling freight would cut them.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** India is a good, integrated business, but it is not a growth story. We model revenue +7% / +6% / +8% (FY27-29E) and an EBITDA margin of 21% / 19.5% / 20%, i.e. Q1's windfall fades to near management's 18-20%. Sep-28E EBITDA ₹1,126 cr is barely above FY26's ₹954 cr plus the new salt plants; the street (Motilal Oswal ₹1,344 cr for FY28E) assumes margins near 24%, well above what management itself calls sustainable.

sections.title: US: the world's cheapest soda ash, earning US$1 a tonne

blocks.p: Green River, Wyoming, sits on the world's largest trona deposits; mining and refining trona uses far less energy than the synthetic process, so TCNA is one of the lowest-cost producers anywhere. That did not protect it. A large part of its volume is exported (the company has not yet given the split), and export prices are set by Chinese ash. EBITDA fell from ₹1,269 cr in FY23 to ₹294 cr in FY26 and ₹3 cr in Q1FY27 (US$1 a tonne, from US$41 a year earlier), even though volumes rose 13% to 614 kt. In Q4FY26 the company wrote off ₹1,837 cr (US$208 mn) of US goodwill and ₹182 cr of deferred tax assets.

bullets: **Exports:** sales to South-East Asia are "just at breakeven level or unremunerative, and that is likely to remain so at least through the year"; US producers have "more or less vacated" that market to China. TCNA is redirecting tonnes to Latin America (lithium) and North-East Asia.
**Domestic US:** stable demand and prices ("a USD 3-4 shift here and there"); logistics costs rising and only partly passed on.

**Searles Valley contracts:** on 11-Sep-2026 TCNA completed the purchase of Searles Valley Minerals' soda ash customer contracts (more than 0.5 mt over two years) from its Chapter 11 process. Price and margin were not disclosed; we add ~6% to FY28E US revenue for it.
**Minority:** US EBITDA includes the ALCAD partnership, 50% owned by a partner who receives ~₹99 cr a year of profit (FY26). We deduct that share in the valuation.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** we assume the US stays close to break-even in FY27 (2.5% EBITDA margin, ~₹135 cr) and recovers only partly to 7% / 9% in FY28-29E (roughly US$15-20/t, versus US$40/t in FY25). The street is far more optimistic (Motilal Oswal ₹760 cr for FY28E, JM ₹769 cr for Sep-27E). We would need to see Chinese capacity actually close before modelling a return to FY24-25 levels.

bullets: **UK (Tata Chemicals Europe).** Soda ash at Lostock stopped in Jan-2025 after years of losses; the UK now makes salt (430 KTPA), pharma salt (70 KTPA, new) and bicarb (90 KTPA) from imported TCNA ash. FY26 revenue fell 27% to ₹1,461 cr but EBITDA rose to ₹88 cr on a lower cost base; it still lost ₹202 cr before tax. Q1FY27 EBITDA was −₹5 cr after ~GBP2.4 mn of one-offs; management expects a positive FY27 EBITDA. The UK also carries most of the group's pension deficit; a 2025-27 support agreement defers payments, and the sale of Winnington land after 2027 is meant to reduce it.

**Kenya (Magadi).** Natural soda ash, mostly exported to Asia. EBITDA fell from ₹468 cr (FY23) to ₹101 cr (FY26) and ₹1 cr in Q1FY27 as export prices fell and heavy fuel oil costs jumped (hedged only to October). A world-first 50 kt electric calciner started in FY26. A ₹891 cr land-rates claim by Kajiado County was rejected by Kenya's Court of Appeal in Oct-2025; the county has appealed to the Supreme Court.
**Singapore (Novabay).** A 60 KTPA pharma-grade bicarb plant bought in Mar-2026 (price not disclosed); Q1FY27 revenue ₹60 cr, EBITDA ₹5 cr. A 40 KTPA expansion is planned (no date).

blocks.callout: **Our view:** together these three units should earn ~₹249 cr of EBITDA on a Sep-28E basis, about 10% of the group. We value them at 5-8x EBITDA. The UK is now a stable, low-margin salt and bicarb business; Kenya swings with export prices and fuel.

sections.title: Half the market value is shares in other companies

blocks.p: Tata Chemicals is partly a holding company. At the 30-Sep-2026 closes, its stakes in listed Tata companies were worth ~₹8,297 cr (₹326 a share) and its 55.04% of Rallis India ₹2,137 cr (₹84 a share): together ₹409 a share, 67% of the ₹611 share price, before any holding-company discount. Titan alone is ₹249 a share. These stakes pay dividends (part of the ~₹300 cr of yearly other income) but are not part of the chemicals business.

First, on the street's method about ₹330 a share of value (after the 20% discount) comes from shares that Tata Chemicals does not control and will probably never sell; it moves with Titan's share price. Second, the Tata Sons stake is a free option at today's price: worth a lot if Tata Sons lists, nothing if it does not. Neither changes the fact that the chemicals business is earning very little.

blocks.callout: **Honest verdict:** Tata Chemicals has good assets but no moat that protects profits. Its US and Kenyan mines are low-cost, yet in a world of Chinese oversupply low cost only means losing less. India is the one market where it has structural advantages (scale, integration, import-parity pricing), and that is where it earns its money. Group ROCE of 3% in FY26 and a US goodwill write-down are the evidence.

sections.title: Ten years of going nowhere: revenue up 41%, profit down to a loss

blocks.p: Tata Chemicals' revenue was ₹10,346 cr in FY17 and ₹14,584 cr in FY26: about 4% a year, and almost all of it came in one jump (FY22-23) when soda ash prices spiked after COVID. EBITDA (operating profit) was ₹2,097 cr in FY17, peaked at ₹3,820 cr in FY23 and has fallen every year since, to ₹1,805 cr in FY26. Profit for shareholders tells a worse story. Leave out FY20, inflated by the demerger of the consumer business into Tata Consumer Products (₹6,480 cr of other income that year), and profit was ₹2,317 cr at the FY23 peak, ₹268 cr in FY24, ₹235 cr in FY25 and a loss of ₹1,896 cr in FY26 after a ₹1,837 cr write-down of US goodwill.

blocks.callout: **So what:** this is a commodity business on a rising cost base. Depreciation went from ₹512 cr (FY17) to ₹1,201 cr (FY26) as capacity was added in India, the UK and Kenya, and interest is ~₹590 cr a year. With EBITDA at ₹1,805 cr, only ~₹15 cr was left before other income in FY26. Minorities (44.96% of Rallis, 50% of a US partnership) then take ~₹180 cr a year. That is why a ₹14,600 cr revenue company earns almost nothing for its shareholders at the bottom of the soda ash cycle.

sections.title: ₹12,800 cr of capex in ten years, and returns are at 3%

blocks.p: Over FY17-26 the group generated ₹21,460 cr of operating cash and spent ₹12,817 cr on capex and ₹4,308 cr on dividends. That is better cash discipline than many chemical companies: free cash flow was positive in nine of the ten years (FY25 was −₹244 cr). The problem is what the capex earned. Return on capital employed (ROCE) was 12% at the FY23 peak and 3% in FY26, against a cost of capital of ~11%. FY24-25 capex (₹3,840 cr) went into the Mithapur soda ash and bicarb expansions, a UK salt plant and Kenya; the new volumes arrived just as prices fell. The 2008 US acquisition (General Chemical, Green River) was written down by ₹1,837 cr (US$208 mn) in FY26: management's own admission that it no longer earns its cost.

sections.title: Earnings quality: minorities, other income and an exceptional item every year

bullets: **Minorities.** Screener's "net profit" is before minorities. Rallis (44.96%) and the ALCAD US partnership (50%) took ₹181 cr in FY26 and ₹77 cr in Q1FY27. In Q1FY27 the group made ₹60 cr before minorities and −₹17 cr after. This report always uses profit after minorities.

**Other income carries the P&L.** FY26 pre-tax profit before exceptional items was ₹497 cr; other income and JV profit were ~₹483 cr of it (dividends from Titan and other Tata shares, interest, IMACID and Tata Industries). Operations alone roughly broke even after depreciation and interest.

**An exceptional item every year.** FY24: ₹963 cr in the UK; FY25: ₹125 cr of Lostock closure costs; FY26: ₹1,956 cr (US goodwill ₹1,837 cr, labour codes ₹54 cr, UK ₹65 cr) plus a US deferred-tax write-off (₹182 cr in the deck, ₹159 cr on the call).
**Smaller items.** Q1FY27 staff cost included a ~₹43 cr one-off benefit; US mining rights (Ind AS only) are amortised at ~₹100 cr a year; FX on overseas loans added ₹460 cr to debt in FY26.
**Audit and disclosure.** B S R & Co. (KPMG network), clean opinion. Unit-wise P&L every quarter is better disclosure than most peers.

blocks.callout: **Accounting flag: AMBER.** Nothing suggests aggressive accounting and disclosure is good, but reported profit is hard to read: minorities, JV income, dividends from strategic stakes and a large exceptional item every year sit between EBITDA and EPS. Investors should look at unit EBITDA and cash flow, not headline profit.

sections.title: Net debt of ~₹6,000 cr against shares in Titan and other Tata companies worth ₹8,300 cr

blocks.p: Screener shows Tata Chemicals with more cash and investments than debt, but that is because it counts the group's stakes in Titan, Indian Hotels, Tata Steel and other Tata companies (₹7,229 cr at March 2026) as cash. They are long-held strategic stakes, not cash the business uses. On the company's own definition, net debt (excluding leases) was ₹5,961 cr at March 2026, up from ₹4,884 cr a year earlier (₹460 cr of it from the weaker rupee on overseas loans), and ₹5,692 cr in June 2026 after selling some land and shares. That is ~4x FY26 EBITDA excluding Rallis: high for a cyclical business. Credit ratings are still strong (CARE and CRISIL AA+/Stable) because of the Tata parentage and the investment portfolio.

FY29 +8%: precipitated silica (Q4FY28, under review) and the 210 KTPA Valinokkam salt plant (Q2FY29).
segments._marginWhy: FY26 19.7%; Q1FY27 28.4% included low-cost coal inventory. Management calls ~18% sustainable; coal, limestone and freight costs rise if the Middle East conflict runs past October. FY27 21% (Q1 actual, ~19% for Q2-Q4); FY28 19.5%; FY29 20% as salt and silica add higher-margin volume.

segments.name: US (Tata Chemicals North America)
segments._why: FY26 revenue -6% (exports to South-East Asia cut, lower prices). Q1FY27 +16% on volumes (614 kt) and a weaker rupee. FY27 +9%; FY28 +6% as the Searles Valley customer contracts bought on 11-Sep-2026 (more than 0.5 mt over two years) add volume; FY29 +2%.
segments._marginWhy: EBITDA margin fell from 24% (FY23) to 6% (FY26) and 0.2% in Q1FY27 (US$1/t) as Chinese export prices (US$160-180/t FOB) made SE Asia exports unremunerative 'at least through the year'. FY27 2.5% (~Rs45 cr a quarter after Q1); FY28 7% and FY29 9% (roughly US$15-20/t) on domestic contract volumes and slow Chinese rationalisation, still far below the US$40/t of FY25-Q1FY26.

segments.name: UK (Tata Chemicals Europe)
segments._why: Since the Lostock soda ash plant closed (Jan-2025) the UK sells salt, pharma salt and bicarb made from imported TCNA ash; FY26 revenue -27% on the closure. Q1FY27 +6%. FY27 +8% (sterling, new pharma salt volumes); 4% a year after.
segments._marginWhy: FY26 6.0%; Q1FY27 -1% after ~GBP2.4 mn of one-offs (EU ETS sale loss, prior-period items). Management expects the UK to be EBITDA positive in FY27. 5% / 7% / 8%.

segments.name: Kenya (Magadi)
segments._why: Natural soda ash exported mainly to Asia; FY26 revenue -4%; Q1FY27 +7% on volumes. 3% a year.
segments._marginWhy: FY23 50%, FY26 17%, Q1FY27 1% as HFO fuel costs jumped with oil (hedged only to October) and export prices fell. FY27 10%; FY28-29 15-16% if fuel normalises, below the FY24-26 average of ~25%.

segments.name: Singapore (Novabay)
segments._why: Premium pharma-grade bicarb plant (60 KTPA) acquired 19-Mar-2026, consolidated from 1-Jan-2026, so FY26 holds one quarter (Rs61 cr). Q1FY27 revenue Rs60 cr: FY27 ~Rs245 cr (+300% on one quarter), then +5% a year; the 40 KTPA expansion has no date yet.
segments._marginWhy: Q1FY27 EBITDA Rs5 cr (8%); integration under way. 8-10%.

segments.name: Rallis India (100%)
segments._why: Crop protection and seeds; FY26 revenue +9%, Q1FY27 +7% (volumes and prices). 8-9% a year, in line with its FY22-26 range.
segments._marginWhy: FY26 12.6%; Q1FY27 18% (seasonal peak); FY23-26 range 7-13%. 13.5-14%. Tata Chemicals owns 55.04%; the 44.96% minority is deducted in the tax line.

segments.name: Inter-company and other adjustments
segments._why: Consolidated revenue less the sum of units: -Rs188 cr in FY26 (UK buys TCNA soda ash, SPV and other adjustments); Q1FY27 -Rs50 cr. Grows with the units.
segments._marginWhy: Zero: the EBITDA difference between consolidated and units was Rs+4 cr in FY26 and Rs+2 cr in Q1FY27.

assumptions._unallocLabel: Corporate costs not in any unit (India standalone carries head office)
assumptions._unallocWhy: Head-office costs sit inside the India standalone numbers; consolidated EBITDA equalled the sum of units within Rs4 cr in FY26.
assumptions._capexWhy: FY26 Rs1,205 cr. FY27: ~Rs1,300 cr guided in May, then 'around depreciation' (~Rs1,200 cr) in July: Rs1,250 cr. FY28-29: maintenance (~Rs800-900 cr) plus the Rs1,525 cr project list (IVSD Rs100 cr, dense ash Rs135 cr, silica Rs775 cr, Valinokkam Rs515 cr) phased over FY27-29; management intends to stay at or below depreciation.
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation Rs1,201 cr = 4.2% of average gross block (Rs28,610 cr); Q1FY27 Rs336 cr (Rs1,344 cr annualised) after capitalisation. 4.4% lands FY27 at ~Rs1,350 cr. Includes ~Rs100 cr a year amortisation of US mining rights.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Net debt company; other income entered separately.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Gross other income + share of JV profit: FY26 Rs483 cr (Rs316 cr other income incl. dividends from Titan and other Tata stakes, Rs167 cr JV share from IMACID and Tata Industries); Q1FY27 Rs39 cr (IMACID shut on sulphur costs, JV share -Rs17 cr). FY27E gross ~Rs350 cr (other income ~Rs250 cr, JV ~Rs100 cr as IMACID restarts), FY28E Rs420 cr, FY29E Rs440 cr (back near FY25-26 levels). Engine workaround for FY27E only: the group makes a loss after tax and minorities while pre-tax profit is close to zero, which a tax rate cannot express, so FY27E 'other income' is shown NET of tax on profitable units (~Rs122 cr: India, Rallis, Kenya, less a US credit) and minorities (~Rs217 cr), i.e. 350 - 122 - 217 = 11, with a zero tax rate.
assumptions._interestWhy: FY26 Rs590 cr; Q1FY27 Rs148 cr. Management expects FY27 debt near Mar-26 levels (net debt ex-leases Rs5,961 cr; Rs5,692 cr in Jun-26).
assumptions._taxWhy: The tax line also carries minorities (engine workaround, as in UPL and Coromandel): Rallis 44.96% (~Rs117-148 cr a year) and the ALCAD US partnership 50% (~Rs99 cr in FY26). Tax itself is paid by India, Rallis and Kenya while UK losses earn no credit and the US books only a partial credit after the Rs182 cr DTA write-off. FY27E: 0% because tax and minorities are netted in other income (see _otherIncomeWhy). FY28E: tax ~Rs190 cr + minorities ~Rs235 cr on PBT ~Rs605 cr = 70%. FY29E: ~Rs240 cr + ~Rs248 cr on ~Rs900 cr = 54%. The DCF applies the FY29E rate to all later years, i.e. it values only Tata Chemicals' share of cash flows and assumes US losses stay untaxed: conservative.
assumptions._payoutWhy: DPS Rs11 for FY25 and FY26 (119% of FY25 EPS; paid despite the FY26 loss). FY27E: 0% in the model because EPS is negative; the Rs11 FY26 dividend paid in FY27 (Rs280 cr) is deducted separately in the SOTP. FY28E 100% of EPS (~Rs7) and FY29E 70% (~Rs11): we assume the board cuts the dividend while the group earns little.

dcf._betaWhy: The engine discounts at one rate (cost of equity = WACC). Tata Chemicals carries debt, so we enter a WACC: cost of equity ~13.1% (beta 1.1) weighted ~72%, post-tax cost of debt ~5.6% weighted ~28% (net debt incl. leases ~Rs6,800 cr vs ~Rs15,600 cr market value) = ~11.0%, which beta 0.75 produces.
dcf._tgWhy: Soda ash, salt and bicarb demand grows with nominal GDP in India and slower abroad; 5% nominal.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Group revenue growth fades to 6% (India 8-9%, overseas 2-3%).
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex fades to 6% of revenue (maintenance ~Rs800-900 cr); depreciation 6.5% of revenue (FY26 8.2%, falling as revenue grows on a mature asset base). Long-run EBITDA margin 16%: the FY22-26 average was 17.6% (peak 22.8% in FY23, trough 12.4% in FY26).

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: China rationalises capacity and export prices recover towards US$220-250/t; the US earns US$30-40/t again with the Searles Valley volumes; India holds 21-22% margins; Kenya fuel costs normalise; Tata Sons lists, giving value to the 2.53% stake (we add Rs5,000 cr, half the low end of press estimates).

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: Chinese oversupply persists through FY29: US EBITDA stays near US$10/t, Kenya margins stay low, India slips to 17-18% as new bicarb capacity and imports compete and coal/limestone costs stay high, and Rallis margins revert to ~12%; no Tata Sons listing.

parts.name: India (standalone)
parts.metricLabel: Sep-28E EBITDA (½ FY28E + ½ FY29E) × EV/EBITDA
parts.note: Street 7x (Motilal Oswal, FY28E) to 9x (JM Financial, Sep-27E). GHCL, the closest Indian soda ash peer, trades at ~5x trailing; DCM Shriram ~9.4x. 8x: a premium to GHCL for salt, bicarb and prebiotics (~45% of India revenue, stickier food/pharma demand), no more because returns are below the cost of capital.

parts.name: US (TCNA)
parts.note: Street 5x (Motilal Oswal) to 6.5x (JM). Low-cost natural soda ash, but price-taker against Chinese exports; Sep-28E EBITDA already assumes a partial recovery from ~zero. 6x.

parts.name: UK (TCE)
parts.note: Street 5x (Motilal Oswal, Europe+Africa) to 8x (JM). Salt and bicarb only since Lostock closed; thin margins and a pension deficit: 5x.

parts.name: Kenya (Magadi)
parts.note: Street 5x (Motilal Oswal) to 6.5x (JM). Exporter of natural ash into the most competitive Asian markets; fuel-cost exposed: 5x.

parts.name: Singapore (Novabay)
parts.note: Pharma-grade bicarb, customer-approved and stickier than soda ash; small (~Rs25 cr EBITDA). Valued like India: 8x.

parts.name: Rallis India: 55.04% stake at market value less 20%
parts.metricLabel: 55.04% × Rs3,883 cr market value (Rs199.73 on 30-Sep-2026) × (1 − discount)
parts.note: Street method (Motilal Oswal, JM: 20% holding-company discount). Bull 10%, bear 30% discount. Rallis EBITDA is therefore not valued again, and its 44.96% minority is not deducted again.

parts.name: Quoted Tata-group shares at market value less 20%
parts.metricLabel: Rs8,297 cr at 30-Sep-2026 closes (Titan Rs6,342 cr, Indian Hotels Rs865 cr, Tata Steel Rs570 cr, others Rs520 cr) × (1 − discount)
parts.note: Mar-26 holdings (AR FY26) at NSE closes on 30-Sep-2026; Tata Investment at Mar-26 book. Street: 20% discount (Motilal Oswal, JM); bull 10%, bear 30%. Some shares were sold in Q1FY27 (undisclosed): a small overstatement.

parts.name: Less: quoted shares at Mar-26 book (inside model net cash)
parts.metricLabel: Removes the book value already counted in the model's cash and investments
parts.note: The model's net cash includes all investments at Mar-26 book; the quoted shares are valued separately above. JVs (IMACID, Tata Industries, Rs1,460 cr), unquoted stakes (incl. Tata Sons at Rs57 cr) and liquid funds stay at book.

parts.name: Tata Sons stake (2.53%)
parts.metricLabel: Only in the bull case: Rs10,000 cr (low end of press estimates) less 50%
parts.note: No listing date: RBI rejected Tata Sons' de-registration on 11-Sep-2026, but Tata Trusts proposed a restructuring that could avoid listing (29-Sep-2026). No broker values it. Base and bear carry it at book (Rs57 cr, inside net cash).

parts.name: Less: Rallis net cash (belongs to Rallis' market value)
parts.metricLabel: Rallis Mar-26 cash Rs45 cr + investments Rs505 cr − borrowings Rs61 cr
parts.note: Rallis is valued at market, which already includes its cash; removing it from consolidated net cash avoids counting it twice.

parts.name: Less: ALCAD partner's 50% (US minority)
parts.metricLabel: Partner's share of profit (Rs99 cr in FY26) × the US multiple
parts.note: US EBITDA includes 100% of the ALCAD partnership; half of its profit belongs to the partner (AR FY26 note 18).

parts.name: Less: employee-benefit provisions (Mar-26)
parts.metricLabel: Consolidated pension and other employee-benefit provisions (AR FY26 note 21)
parts.note: Mostly UK and US pension deficits; the street deducts the same (Motilal Oswal Rs1,198 cr, JM Rs1,203 cr).

parts.name: Less: FY26 dividend paid in FY27
parts.note: Paid in Q2FY27; the model books no FY27 dividend because FY27E EPS is negative.

parts.name: Net cash at Sep-27E (model: cash and investments less borrowings incl. leases)
parts.note: Mar-26: cash Rs442 cr + investments Rs9,886 cr − borrowings incl. leases Rs8,001 cr = +Rs2,327 cr; after removing quoted shares at book this is net debt of ~Rs4,900 cr incl. leases and JVs at book.

methods.name: Sum of the parts
methods.why: How the street values Tata Chemicals (Motilal Oswal, JM Financial, Kotak): four geographies with very different economics, a listed subsidiary and a portfolio of Tata-group shares worth about half the market value.

methods.name: Group EV/EBITDA
methods.why: 7.3x = our own one-year-forward EV/EBITDA median since Apr-2021 (8.6x, trough year FY26 left out) less the 15% median de-rating of Indian commodity chemical peers; bull = the 8.6x median, bear = the 6.1x the stock traded at on 30-Sep-2026 (FY28E). One multiple on consolidated EBITDA (incl. 100% of Rallis), plus model net cash with all investments at book. Rougher than the SOTP: no holding-company discount on investments, no deduction for minorities or pensions.

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: 15-year FCFF at ~11% WACC, terminal growth 5%, plus model net cash (investments at book).
